visual: Compact variegated shrub with green and golden-yellow foliage that develops orange and red tones in autumn, plus small fragrant pink-tinted white flowers.
water: Water regularly while establishing; once established, water during prolonged dry periods.
aspect: Full sun; best in a sheltered east-, south- or west-facing position.
soil: Fertile, moist but well-drained chalk, loam or sandy soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged soil; winter wet and exposed cold positions can reduce vigour and leaf retention.
prune: Lightly trim from spring to late summer to shape; remove any vigorous reverted shoots. Older plants can be renovated more firmly if required.
hardinessNote: Hardy through most of the UK; may become semi-evergreen or lose more foliage during colder winters.
resilience: Drought tolerant once established and generally pest-free; may be susceptible to honey fungus.
uses: Low shrub border, patio container, foliage colour, informal hedge, courtyard and wildlife-friendly planting.

visual: Low evergreen shrub with narrow intensely silver-grey foliage and masses of pink-flushed buds opening to white funnel-shaped flowers with yellow centres.
water: Water moderately during active growth and while establishing; established plants prefer relatively dry conditions and should be kept drier in winter.
aspect: Full sun; sheltered south- or west-facing position.
soil: Very well-drained chalk, loam or sandy soil of low to moderate fertility; tolerant of acid, neutral or alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Excellent drainage is essential, particularly in winter; cold wet soil is a greater risk than summer dryness.
prune: Lightly trim after flowering to maintain a compact shape; avoid cutting heavily into old woody growth.
hardinessNote: Hardy through most of the UK in a warm, sheltered and sharply drained position; vulnerable to prolonged cold combined with winter wet.
resilience: Heat and drought tolerant once established and generally pest-free; occasional honey fungus has been recorded.
uses: Mediterranean planting, gravel garden, sunny border, raised bed and patio container.
uncertain: SENSE appears in commercial trade listings for Convolvulus cneorum, but an authoritative registered cultivar identity could not be confirmed; size and care data therefore follow the species.

visual: Compact cyclamen with marbled dark-green foliage and unusual upward-facing open pink flowers with a darker central eye and contrasting crested beard.
water: Water from below when the compost begins to dry, allow excess water to drain fully and reduce watering substantially during dormancy.
aspect: Bright filtered light or partial shade; cool and sheltered.
soil: Well-drained potting compost with good aeration; tolerant of a range of pH provided drainage is excellent.
soilWarning: Do not leave the tuber or crown sitting wet and avoid repeatedly wetting the crown, foliage and flowers; waterlogging readily causes rot.
prune: Deadhead promptly by removing each spent flower and its entire stem cleanly back to the base.
toxicity: Tubers are harmful if eaten and the plant should be kept away from pets and children; wear gloves if sensitive when handling.
hardinessNote: Tolerates cool temperatures but not significant frost; primarily suited to cool indoor conditions, conservatories or frost-protected outdoor positions in the UK.
resilience: Long-flowering and bred for strong pot performance, but vulnerable to excessive heat, waterlogging, cyclamen mite, thrips, aphids and grey mould.
uses: Flowering houseplant, cool conservatory, sheltered porch, seasonal patio pot and indoor winter colour.
uncertain: RHS currently records the horticultural name status of Cyclamen persicum 'Illusia' as unresolved, although the plant is confirmed as Schoneveld's Illusia introduction.

visual: Upright evergreen shrub with dark glossy foliage and single autumn flowers that fade from vivid lavender-pink margins through pale pink to a white centre.
water: Keep evenly moist while establishing and during summer bud formation; container plants require regular watering, preferably with rainwater in hard-water areas.
aspect: Full sun or partial shade; sheltered east-, south- or west-facing position.
soil: Humus-rich, acidic, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid alkaline or chalky soil, waterlogging and prolonged summer drought; cold drying winds can damage developing buds and flowers.
prune: Little pruning is normally required; lightly shape immediately after flowering and remove damaged or congested shoots.
hardinessNote: Hardy through most of the UK in a suitable sheltered position, though flowers and buds can be damaged by severe frost or cold winds.
resilience: Tolerates more sun than many camellias once established but remains sensitive to alkaline soil and drought; possible pests include aphids, scale insects and vine weevil.
uses: Autumn and winter flowering specimen, sheltered border, wall-side planting, courtyard and large container.

visual: Clump-forming perennial with striking bright lime-green foliage and slender upright stems carrying creamy-white flowers in spring and summer.
water: Keep moderately and consistently moist, particularly after planting and in containers, while allowing excess water to drain freely.
aspect: Partial shade or full shade; suitable for most aspects in a sheltered position.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained clay, loam or sandy soil; acid to neutral.
soilWarning: Avoid persistent waterlogging. Older crowns tend to rise above the soil and benefit from division and replanting with the crown remaining just above ground level.
prune: No formal pruning required; remove tired foliage and spent flower stems as necessary and divide ageing clumps periodically.
hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK; container-grown plants are somewhat more vulnerable during severe freezes.
resilience: Cold hardy and reasonably drought resistant once established, although best growth occurs with consistent moisture; susceptible to vine weevil, eelworm and heuchera rust.
uses: Shady border, ground cover, woodland-style planting, rose and shrub underplanting, banks and containers.

visual: Dense upright evergreen camellia with green leaves edged or marked pale yellow and elegant single white flowers with conspicuous pink to reddish-pink margins.
water: Keep evenly moist while establishing and during summer bud development; use rainwater where tap water is strongly alkaline.
aspect: Full sun or partial shade in a sheltered position.
soil: Humus-rich, acidic, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Lime-sensitive; avoid alkaline soil, waterlogging and severe summer drying, particularly while flower buds are developing.
prune: Usually requires little pruning; lightly shape after flowering and remove dead, damaged or badly placed growth.
hardinessNote: Hardy through most of the UK when sheltered, although exposed frost and cold winds can damage flowers and young growth.
resilience: Evergreen and relatively tolerant of sun once established; the main vulnerabilities are unsuitable alkaline soil, drought and common camellia pests or root diseases.
uses: Autumn-flowering specimen, foliage feature, sheltered border, courtyard, wall-side planting and large container.
uncertain: The shorter name Camellia sasanqua 'Variegata' is treated by RHS as a synonym of the accepted cultivar name 'Sasanqua Variegata'.

visual: Dwarf clump-forming saxifrage with rosettes of scalloped dark purple-green leaves and masses of delicate star-like pink and white flowers with yellow centres in autumn.
water: Keep evenly moist during active growth but allow excess water to drain freely; container plants should not be allowed to dry completely.
aspect: Partial shade or full shade; sheltered east-, south- or west-facing position.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sandy soil; tolerant of acid, neutral or alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged conditions and prolonged hot, dry exposure; performs best with cool roots and reliable moisture.
prune: No pruning required; spent flower stems and damaged leaves can be removed for appearance.
hardinessNote: Hardy through most of the UK when grown in moist but well-drained soil and protected from severe exposure.
resilience: Generally disease-free but can be affected by aphids, slugs, vine weevil and glasshouse red spider mite.
uses: Shady border, woodland planting, rock garden, autumn container display and cool indoor display.
uncertain: Dancing Pixies Tini is the trade designation; RHS lists 'Sh 1914' as the cultivar synonym.

visual: Compact evergreen shrub with small glossy spine-tipped dark-green leaves, tiny white bell-shaped flowers and conspicuous white berries on pollinated female plants.
water: Keep consistently moist, especially while establishing and when grown in sun or containers.
aspect: Partial shade or full shade; can tolerate sunnier positions where the soil remains consistently moist.
soil: Acidic to neutral, humus-rich or naturally peaty, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Lime-sensitive. Female plants generally require a compatible male Gaultheria mucronata nearby for reliable berry production.
prune: Requires little pruning; lightly shape if necessary and remove unwanted suckers where spreading needs to be restricted.
toxicity: Berries are grown as ornamental fruit and should not be eaten; keep ornamental berries away from pets and children.
hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK, although plants in exposed containers may benefit from protection during severe freezes.
resilience: Cold hardy, wind tolerant and generally pest-free; naturally suckering and may be susceptible to honey fungus where the disease is already present.
uses: Autumn and winter berry display, acid border, container, woodland-style planting, coastal garden and low evergreen ground cover.
uncertain: The supplied label 'Gaultheria muc. WHITE' appears to indicate a white-fruited Gaultheria mucronata selection, but an authoritative cultivar named simply 'White' could not be verified.
White-fruited forms occur within Gaultheria mucronata, so species-level cultivation data have been used.

visual: Compact mound-forming perennial producing large semi-double deep-red flowers broadly tipped golden yellow, often with warm orange transitional colouring.
water: Water regularly while establishing; once established, allow the soil to dry somewhat between waterings and irrigate mainly during prolonged drought.
aspect: Full sun; open or sheltered sunny position.
soil: Moderately fertile, sharply well-drained soil; performs particularly well in sandy, gravelly or chalky conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid heavy waterlogged ground, especially over winter; excessive fertility or moisture can produce soft growth and reduce longevity.
prune: Deadhead regularly to encourage continuous flowering; cut back spent growth after flowering or tidy remaining old stems in early spring.
hardinessNote: A hardy perennial suitable for most UK gardens when drainage is good; winter wet is likely to be a greater limitation than cold in many sites.
resilience: Heat and drought tolerant once established, tolerant of coastal conditions and highly attractive to pollinating insects.
uses: Sunny border, gravel garden, wildlife garden, coastal planting, cut flowers and patio container.
uncertain: Danziger lists GUSTO Sweet Chili at Gaillardia genus/series level rather than assigning a species; some UK retailers describe it as Gaillardia × hybrida.
H5 is a conservative UK garden hardiness estimate based on comparable perennial Gaillardia cultivars; breeder information lists the GUSTO series for USDA zones 4–9.
